Taking a look at the REST APIs here: https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/#/Validator/get_validator_duties__epoch__attester I am curious how frozen those are? Specifically I'm looking at the `validator_pubkeys` which is submitted via a URL parameter. Curerntly it is expected to be a single parameter, with multiple public keys encoded as an array with `,` as separators. Given that url parameters can be provided multiple times, it seems cleaner to have them just be submitted individually - current: `/validator/duties/<epoch>/attester?validator_pubkeys=key1,key2,key3` - what I'm proposing: `validator/duties/<epoch>/attester?validator_pukkey=key1&validator_pubkey=key2&validator_pubkey=key3` The benefit of this approach is that web frameworks, both server and client will handle this natively. The current approach requires both client and server to do a little bit of extra parsing/validation. I ran into this myself and would support this change Next step is prolly just a PR, these aren’t as frozen as say the consensus spec I'll work on getting a PR open and discussion can continue there if it doesn't get kaboshed here for some reason Where does it say, delimited? If you try endpoint you will see its formed like you said Maybe a different api version? I know the older version wanted keys packed into a comma sep array Oh, interesting, I think the spec is correct and does use things the way I was proposing, I was just reading the swagger docs wrong https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-APIs/blob/master/apis/validator/duties.yaml#L14 The naming of the parameter is what confused me the most (since the parameter name is plural). I can see arguments for both naming conventions so nothing wrong there, everyone carry on. thanks <@!545555441518772225> yeah, makes sense to make it singular 👍 but naming of endpoints is being changed with complete proposal so thisng might also get changed

excerpts.content:
Not sure this is the right channel but... Taking a look at the REST APIs here: https://ethereum.github.io/eth2.0-APIs/#/Validator/get_validator_duties__epoch__attester

I am curious how frozen those are?  Specifically I'm looking at the `validator_pubkeys` which is submitted via a URL parameter.  Curerntly it is expected to be a single parameter, with multiple public keys encoded as an array with `,` as separators.  Given that url parameters can be provided multiple times, it seems cleaner to have them just be submitted individually

- current: `/validator/duties/<epoch>/attester?validator_pubkeys=key1,key2,key3`
- what I'm proposing: `validator/duties/<epoch>/attester?validator_pukkey=key1&validator_pubkey=key2&validator_pubkey=key3`

The benefit of this approach is that web frameworks, both server and client will handle this natively.  The current approach requires both client and server to do a little bit of extra parsing/validation.
